evidence.summary: CatBoost achieved R² 0.8666, indicating substantial non-linear structure.
Account age had the strongest positive observed association with score, with Spearman correlation +0.816. Controlled observations also showed score increasing as account age increased.
Months active had a strong negative association with score, with Spearman correlation -0.807. Controlled configurations also showed a negative effect.

Trust score had a negative overall Spearman association of -0.732, but controlled observations showed high scores around 345–355 and lower scores at substantially larger values, ruling out a simple higher-is-better relationship.
Utilisation had a positive overall Spearman association of +0.657. Controlled observations also showed measurable score changes as utilisation changed.
Channel affected observed scores, with channel D producing some of the highest observed scores, but its effect was weaker than the main numerical features.
CatBoost achieved R² 0.8666, MAE 0.0579, and RMSE 0.1030, making it the strongest tested model for score reconstruction.
Logistic Regression with StandardScaler achieved ROC-AUC 0.9772 and Average Precision 0.9568, showing that the observed features contain strong information about the hidden decision boundary.
The final dataset contains 207 APPROVE and 73 DECLINE observations, providing substantially more decision diversity than an extremely approval-skewed query strategy.
SMOTE was applied only after the train/test split to the training partition. The test set remained untouched.
No individual feature explained the complete observed score or decision behavior.
Linear Regression achieved R² 0.7845, substantially below CatBoost at R² 0.8666, indicating non-linear structure.
The exact mathematical scoring formula has not been recovered despite strong predictive reconstruction.
The exact hidden rule or threshold converting the score into APPROVE or DECLINE has not been established.
